discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution based on the uncertainty principle and on quantum entanglement

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the no-cloning property and the complementarity of quantum measurements can guarantee secret communication: any eavesdropper unavoidably disturbs the quantum states. Ekert (1991) connected security directly to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities, turning a foundational test of quantum mechanics into a cryptographic resource and a basis for device-independent security. Together these ideas founded quantum information science as an experimental discipline. They led to the concepts of quantum teleportation (Bennett et al., 1993) and to decades of experiments: fibre networks spanning thousands of kilometres, measurement-device-independent protocols, and satellite-based entanglement distribution and key exchange between continents. Few theoretical insights have opened so large and so durable an experimental and technological frontier, which the physics community keeps extending. The 2022 Prize recognised entanglement experiments; this prize would honour the conceptual origin of quantum communication.
